metaDescription: Odoo ships no farm app. How crop cycles, harvest lots, grading, cold chain and grower settlement are really built, and the country rules that change it.
intro: Odoo ships no agriculture app. There is no crop record, no field boundary and no growing season in version 17, 18 or 19, and no official app adds one. A farm system is assembled from parts that exist: the block as an analytic account, the crop cycle as a production order or a project, harvest intake as a tracked lot, and grading as a production run with by-products. Anything sold as an Odoo farm module is third party or bespoke code, and should be priced as code you will own.

The build earns its keep in one place, cost per hectare. Fuel, spray, labour, irrigation and machine hours are spent across many blocks, and the crop then sells as a single number. Analytic plans carry that spend to the block, the season and the crop on the same journal item, so a field that has lost money for three seasons stops hiding inside a profitable farm total. That is the report the owner is actually buying.

Edition matters here. Community already covers lot tracking, expiration dates and FEFO removal, manufacturing with by-products, blanket purchase agreements, landed costs, Fleet, Maintenance, Project, Timesheets and analytic plans. Enterprise adds Quality control points, the Barcode app, IoT, Field Service, Documents and Payroll. Cold store telemetry, weather feeds and weighbridge readings sit in neither edition, and each one arrives as an integration with a cost line of its own.
whoFor: Commercial growers running blocks, orchards or greenhouses where the cost of a season has to land on a field rather than on the whole farm.
Packhouses that take in field lots by weight and ship graded cartons by count, with a different unit at each end of the shed.
Contract farming operations that advance inputs and cash to growers and recover the value against a graded outturn.
Fresh produce exporters who have to assemble lot genealogy and certificates faster than the container moves.
Not for a smallholding selling at a weekly market, where the record keeping Odoo asks for costs more than the visibility it gives back.
Not for precision agriculture: Odoo holds no field geometry, no imagery and no variable rate prescriptions, and it will not become an agronomy platform.

capabilities.title: Blocks, seasons and analytic plans
capabilities.body: Odoo splits analytic accounting into plans, and a farm uses several: one for the block, orchard or greenhouse, one for the season, one for the crop, and one for a grant scheme where public money is involved. A single journal item carries a percentage split across all of them at once, so a diesel bill burnt over four blocks is posted once and lands on four cost centres. Planted area, planting date and variety are custom fields on the analytic account, because Odoo stores no map of your land.

capabilities.title: Crop cycles as production orders or as projects
capabilities.body: Two patterns hold up in practice. A manufacturing order for the season consumes seed, fertiliser and spray as components and produces the harvested crop, which gives real cost roll-up and forces someone to record what was applied. A project per block with tasks and timesheets is lighter, gives the farm manager a calendar he will actually open, and records no material consumption. Many farms run both: orders for inputs and cost, projects for scheduling spray, irrigation and picking crews.

capabilities.title: Intake, lot numbers and yield
capabilities.body: Harvest is received against a lot naming the block, the picking date and the shift. From there the traceability view on that lot walks forward to every carton and every customer it reached. Yield per hectare is produced in a pivot from received quantity over the planted area held on the analytic account, rather than stored as a field on a form. Weighbridge and platform scales do not reach Odoo by themselves. Either the clerk keys the net weight, or the scale is wired through an IoT box, which is Enterprise.

capabilities.title: Grading and packing with by-product cost share
capabilities.body: One intake lot leaves the shed as Class 1, Class 2 and reject. That is a manufacturing order with by-products, each carrying a cost share percentage on the bill of materials, so the value of the intake splits across grades on a ratio you set instead of loading entirely onto the premium line. Packing consumes cartons, liners and labels as components. Produce sold loose by weight and also packed by count is two products with a defined conversion, not one product in two units.

capabilities.title: Expiry dates, FEFO and the cold store
capabilities.body: Turning on expiration dates gives every lot a best before date, a removal date and an alert date, and makes FEFO available as a removal strategy on the location. FEFO is the single change that cuts write-off fastest, because picking follows the oldest saleable lot rather than the nearest pallet. Cold rooms are ordinary stock locations holding real quantities, so a temperature excursion is handled by moving the affected lot into quarantine or scrapping it, and either action leaves an auditable move behind.

capabilities.title: Grower agreements, advances and settlement
capabilities.body: A blanket purchase agreement holds the volume and price agreed with a grower for the season, and each delivery draws against it, so the balance still owed under contract is visible without a spreadsheet. Inputs issued to a grower are recorded against that grower and netted at settlement rather than invoiced as a sale. Cash advances sit as unreconciled vendor payments until the bill is raised. Where growers are paid on graded outturn, the bill waits for the grading order to close.

setup.title: Settle the unit of measure before anything else
setup.body: Odoo converts within a unit category on a fixed ratio, and there is no catch weight on the product. A crate weighing between eight and eleven kilograms therefore cannot be a unit of the kilogram category. The pattern that works is to trade in weight and hold the crate as its own product or as packaging, with the actual weight captured at dispatch. This decision sets every price list, every bill and every historical report, so it is not one to revisit in year two.

setup.title: Design the analytic plans once, then automate the split
setup.body: Agree the plans during design: block, season, crop, and scheme where grant money is involved. Two plans are easy to live with. Five become an entry burden that field staff quietly skip. Analytic distribution models apply a default split by partner, product category or department, so the vehicles, employees and purchase lines that generate most of the postings tag themselves. Retro-fitting analytic distribution across a year of posted entries is manual work that nobody budgets for.

setup.title: A lot number a supervisor can read
setup.body: Left alone, Odoo numbers lots from one running sequence, which tells nobody anything when a crate is standing in front of them. A number encoding block, date and shift can be traced by a person, and it is either keyed at intake by the weighbridge clerk or generated by a small customisation. Decide lot against serial tracking before any stock exists, because changing the tracking setting on a product with moves behind it means clearing that stock first.

setup.title: Costing method and landed cost before the first receipt
setup.body: Set the costing method on the product category before anything is received, because changing it later revalues everything on hand. Average cost suits produce that pools in a bin. FIFO suits lots that stay distinct all the way to the customer. Landed costs push freight, cold store, inspection and clearing charges onto the receipt so the cost of a shipped carton is real. Fair value accounting for a growing crop is not in Odoo and stays a manual year end adjustment.

setup.title: Cut over between seasons, not during one
setup.body: There is no clean import for a half grown crop. Take the cutover in the quiet window if the calendar allows it, count what sits in the cold store and the packhouse, and start flat. Growing costs already spent can be loaded as an opening analytic balance per block so the season still compares against last year. Growers, products, certificates and price lists load and get checked before stock, never in the same week.

pitfalls.title: Yield divided by an area nobody maintains
pitfalls.body: Harvest quantity is easy to capture. Planted area is not. A block gets partly replanted, a corner goes out of production, and the hectare figure in the system is still the one off the title deed. Every yield number then reads optimistic, and the comparison between blocks is quietly wrong. Hold planted area as a dated value per season, and make one named person responsible for updating it at planting rather than at reporting time.

pitfalls.title: One analytic account called Farm
pitfalls.body: The quickest configuration is a single analytic account for the whole operation, and it removes the reason for doing the project at all. Cost per hectare, per crop and per season collapse back into the one number the owner already had. If field staff will not enter a distribution, the answer is default distribution models and a short list of accounts, not giving up on the plan.

pitfalls.title: Grading booked as an inventory adjustment
pitfalls.body: When Class 2 appears as a positive adjustment and the intake as a negative one, the cost of the intake vanishes into a variance account and grade margin can never be recovered afterwards. It also cuts the lot link, so a complaint on a Class 1 carton no longer traces back to a block. Grading is a production step even when nothing is physically transformed, and modelling it as one costs about a minute a day.

pitfalls.title: Lots created at the packing line
pitfalls.body: Numbering produce when it is packed rather than when it is picked loses the field. Two blocks mix in a bin, one lot is created at the line, and the genealogy stops at the shed door. Every recall, buyer audit and residue query then covers a whole day of picking instead of one block. Record the lot at intake and accept that the shed will handle more lot numbers than it would like.

pitfalls.title: Cold chain evidence kept outside the system
pitfalls.body: Temperature charts printed from a data logger and filed in a folder satisfy nobody at an audit and cannot be joined to a shipment. Odoo reads no sensor on its own. Either attach the logger export to the delivery order so the evidence travels with the lot, or build the ingestion properly and pay for it. Deferring the decision is how an exporter ends up running two systems, one of them handwritten.

worksWith: Inventory, for lot tracking, expiration dates, FEFO removal and cold rooms held as real stock locations
Manufacturing, for grading and packing runs where by-products take a share of the intake cost
Purchase, with blanket agreements holding the volume and price agreed per grower for the season
Accounting, for analytic distribution, landed costs and the valuation of stock sitting in the cold store
Fleet and Maintenance, so tractor hours, fuel and service cost land against the block that consumed them
Quality and Barcode in Enterprise, for intake checks and scanning on the packing line
Project, Timesheets and Field Service, for scheduling spray, irrigation and picking crews
Sales and eCommerce, where a farm shop, a box scheme and a wholesale price list share one stock pool

regional.note: ZATCA Phase 2 clears each standard invoice through Fatoora before it reaches the buyer, so a packhouse invoicing on the day of dispatch needs clearance inside the daily flow, not at month end. Food carries the standard 15 percent rate with no zero rating to fall back on. Farm labour is paid through WPS, and Agricultural Development Fund support deserves an analytic plan of its own.

Corporate tax at 9 percent applies above the threshold, and free zone status has to be tested against qualifying income rather than assumed, which matters where a trading arm sits beside the farm. E-invoicing is moving to a Peppol based model on a phased timetable, so partner identifiers and product master data need cleaning early. Most produce work here is re-export and cold chain, with labour paid through WPS.

FBR digital invoicing covers taxable supplies while unprocessed farm produce sits largely outside sales tax, so a business that both grows and processes runs exempt and taxable lines in one ledger and has to apportion input tax. Agricultural income is taxed by the provinces rather than federally, which means farm income and trading income need separate books from day one, not a filter at year end.

Fresh produce is mostly nil rated under GST while the packed and processed line is taxable, so input credit has to be apportioned and reversed against exempt supplies. E-way bill exemptions for agricultural goods vary by state. Sales through an APMC mandi add commission and market fee to the settlement, and a farmer producer organisation reports for its members as well as for itself.

Buying from a registered farmer who issues no invoice means the buyer raises a mustahsil makbuzu and withholds tax at the rate set for that product. Odoo has no equivalent document, and the electronic form runs through the same GIB channel as e-Fatura and e-Arsiv. Produce also cannot legally move until an e-Irsaliye has been issued and accepted, which puts the dispatch step on the network.

Every ETA invoice line needs a registered GS1 or EGS item code, so a new pack size cannot be sold until its code exists, which turns product master work into a blocking task. Horticultural exports need a phytosanitary certificate and registration with the plant quarantine authority, and that certificate number belongs on the shipment record. Imported inputs clear through Nafeza against an ACID number raised before the vessel sails.

Making Tax Digital asks for digital links from record to return, so a VAT figure retyped from a spreadsheet fails even when the number is right. A farm shop sells zero rated food beside standard rated goods, so the rating belongs on the product rather than on the till. In England, delinked payments and Sustainable Farming Incentive agreements are separate income streams and want their own analytic tagging.

Packers and processors commonly issue recipient created tax invoices on behalf of growers, which reverses the normal document direction and is not something Odoo does without work. Statutory commodity levies are deducted at the first point of sale and shown on that same document. Basic food is GST free while packing and freight services are not, and seasonal labour reports through Single Touch Payroll.

faqs.q: Does Odoo have an agriculture or farm management module?
faqs.a: No. There is no crop, field or season record in Odoo 17, 18 or 19, and no official app that adds one. What exists are the parts a farm system is built from: analytic plans, lot tracking and expiry, manufacturing with by-products, purchase agreements, Fleet and Maintenance. Anything marketed as an Odoo farm module is third party or bespoke code, and it should be assessed as code you will end up maintaining.

faqs.q: Can we run this on Odoo Community?
faqs.a: Most of it. Inventory with lots, expiration dates and FEFO, Manufacturing with by-products, blanket purchase agreements, landed costs, Fleet, Maintenance, Project, Timesheets and analytic accounting are all Community. Enterprise adds Quality control points, the Barcode app, IoT for scales and gauges, Field Service, Documents and Payroll. A packhouse scanning at the line and a farm running payroll in the system are the two cases that usually decide it.

faqs.q: How is cost per hectare actually tracked?
faqs.a: Through analytic distribution, not a report written afterwards. The block is an analytic account on one plan and the season sits on a second, and each journal item splits across both by percentage. Fuel, wages, spray, machine time and stock issues all land there. Planted area is a value you maintain per season on the account, and the division happens in a pivot view.

faqs.q: Can Odoo handle catch weight, where a crate sells as one unit but weighs a variable amount?
faqs.a: Not natively. Conversion inside a unit category is a fixed ratio, so a package of varying weight has nowhere to sit on the product. The usual answer is to trade in weight and hold the package as a separate product, capturing the actual weight at dispatch. Where the invoice has to follow the weighed amount line by line, that is a development with a price attached.

faqs.q: Will Odoo monitor cold store temperature?
faqs.a: Not on its own. Odoo holds locations, lots and expiry dates and will quarantine a lot by moving it, but nothing standard reads a sensor. Continuous monitoring stays with the data logger or building management system you already run, connected through the IoT box in Enterprise or through an API feed. Treat it as an integration with its own line in the budget.

faqs.q: How do we pay growers who deliver before a price is agreed?
faqs.a: Receive the crop against the grower at a provisional value so stock is not carrying zero. Advances sit as unreconciled vendor payments. Once the outturn is graded and the price is fixed, the bill is raised on final figures and the advances are matched against it. Where provisional and final values differ, the posting for that difference should be agreed with the accountant during design.

faqs.q: Can we pull weather or satellite data into Odoo?
faqs.a: There is no weather feature and no field imagery in Odoo. Forecast and rainfall data comes from an external service over an API and is stored against the block, so spray windows and irrigation records read alongside it. It is a small build with an ongoing data cost. Confirm that somebody will act on the data before paying for it.

faqs.q: How long does a farm implementation take?
faqs.a: Configuration is measured in weeks. What sets the date is whether blocks, areas and crop plans exist anywhere other than in the farm manager's head, and whether the packhouse will agree to record lots at intake. A single site with clean block data and one crop moves quickly. A grower network of hundreds of suppliers on paper delivery notes is a different project.
